title: Semi-sync cohortless canary with reproducible playback and rollback-oracle
author: Maya Patel
description: Summary: Introduces a new semi-synchronous, cohort-agnostic canary controller plus a rollback-oracle that synthesizes reproducible playback artifacts for fast investigation. Motivation: existing canary primitives require pre-defined cohorts or synchronous promotes which increases blast radius or complicates session affinity. This change lets teams do lightweight, low-latency promotes by mirroring then partially promoting traffic probabilistically without predefining cohorts and with an automated rollback decision path. Design highlights: 1) Semi-sync promote: requests are mirrored to the new model variant and responses are validated by a local compare engine; a configurable fraction of live traffic is then routed (by sampling key hashes) to the candidate variant while still mirroring for auditing. 2) Cohortless selection: traffic slicing uses deterministic hashing of stable request attributes (client_id, user_cookie fallback) with a feature toggle to fall back to randomized sampling for privacy-sensitive endpoints. No pre-provisioned cohort definitions required. 3) Rollback-oracle: when metric gates fail (latency p99, token-error-rate, policy-violation score), the controller builds a rollback artifact bundle that contains: a compact trace summary, the deterministic sampling seed, the canary routing snapshot, and a minimal replay log (hashed request fingerprints + stable inputs) to allow reproducible playback in an offline sandbox. 4) Repro-playback integration: added an API surface to export the rollback bundle to the eval-harness or a local sandbox image so engineers can replay the exact sampled traffic to validate root cause and confirm a fix before re-deploy. 5) Safety gates: configurable multi-metric gates (statistical z-test on success rate, QoS delta threshold for latency and cost-per-token) with timeout windows and an automatic throttle-decay to avoid oscillation. 6) Session-awareness: sticky-key policy preserves session affinity for a configurable window when promoting to avoid user-visible regression for stateful flows. 7) Observability: adds per-promote telemetry: sample_count, sampled_success_rate, p99_delta_ms, rollback_decision_reason, replay_bundle_id. Backwards compatibility: controller defaults keep existing canary semantics unless teams opt-in to the new flow by setting launchPolicy.semiSync = true. Implementation notes: controller changes in rollout-controller service (Go), local compare engine plugin (Rust) compiled as a wasm filter for the data-plane, a light-weight SQL table for storing replay bundle indices (50–200 rows per canary), and an admin API to export bundles. Checklist: - [x] Controller logic and state machine implemented - [x] Compare engine wasm filter + unit tests - [x] Deterministic sampling function + property tests - [x] Rollback bundle export API + ACL check - [x] End-to-end harness integration and replay smoke tests - [x] Telemetry dashboards updated and sample_generator added to canary job - [x] Docs added to rollout playbooks - [x] Load test for semi-sync path at 50k rps simulated traffic Done. Testing: unit tests for sampling, integration tests against eval-harness using the exported bundle, canary simulation in perf-canary repo, and a small staged rollout in a dedicated sandbox cluster. Migration/Upgrade plan: opt-in via launchPolicy toggle; no automatic changes to existing rollouts. Release notes and upgrade guidance are in docs/playbooks/semi-sync-canary.md. Rolling forward: merged to main after sign-offs and can be gated behind feature-flag in production via remote-config.

review_conversation: Srinivas Rao (reviewer): Can you explain why we chose deterministic hashing over cohort definitions? Concern: risk of correlating privacy-sensitive keys.

Maya Patel (author): Deterministic hashing lets us provide sticky sampling for session-affine flows; we added a privacy opt-out that switches to randomized sampling for endpoints marked sensitive. Added tests to validate opt-out behavior.
Claire Ho (reviewer): The rollback bundle contains request fingerprints. Are they reversible?

Maya Patel (author): No, we store salted 128-bit fingerprints and strip PII; the replay bundle includes stable inputs for deterministic cases but not raw user identifiers. Security reviewed by SSO team.
release_notes: Added semi-synchronous cohortless canary controller with deterministic sampling, rollback-artifact export for reproducible playback, and multi-metric automatic rollback oracle. Opt-in via launchPolicy.semiSync. See docs/playbooks/semi-sync-canary.md for rollout guidance.
merge_outcome: merged after approvals from rollout and SRE teams; feature gated behind remote-config; no forced changes to existing rollouts
notes_for_oncall: If semiSync is enabled and a rollback occurs, the controller will emit a replay_bundle_id in logs. Use the eval-harness sandbox to reproduce. If bundles fail export due to SQL contention, increase replay_bundle_index connection pool (default 5).
